recommended_target.loss: event-equal grouped binomial negative log likelihood, normalized by 1/R so replica count buys no scientific weight
recommended_target.object: p(x, tau) = P(task success | robot-local state x, candidate topology tau) under the prospectively frozen disturbance law
recommended_target.observation: k successes out of R matched replicas
recommended_target.runtime: one scalar per candidate; select the larger, hold the committed topology within a frozen near-tie margin

residual_risks: p is defined relative to the frozen uniform-disk disturbance law, not to any real-world disturbance population, and every report must say so
if the evaluation headline drifts from episode task success to calibration, that is hypothesis drift and must be declared
the deterministic families would carry R = 1, so their observation is degenerate at 0 or 1; whether to raise R there is an owner parameter with a real cost
extending the validation variant space touches frozen scenario code
verdict_text: The prospective V3 scientific target is sufficiently specified for an explicit owner decision and freeze phase. The disturbance semantics are resolved from repository authority, the replica-count mathematics is settled, H1 compatibility is established, the reuse and contamination positions are recorded, a complete prospective gate set is drafted with its owner parameters marked, and the compute budget is measured.
what_this_recommendation_is_not: it is not a rescue of V2
it is not designed to make 59/530 pass
it was not chosen for compute savings; fresh generation is affordable at roughly 27 CPU-hours
why_C: the disturbance is an explicitly specified probability distribution and the replicas are iid draws from it, so p(x, tau) is the object the experiment actually measures -- this is a repository fact, not a modelling preference
it is the only option that supervises the stochastic boundary instead of deleting, capping or reclassifying it, and the boundary is where a candidate-conditioned selector has the most to learn
it needs no per-event precision, so modest R remains coherent; consistency comes from the event count
H1 survives verbatim: the primary metric stays EPISODE_TASK_SUCCESS on PAIRED_EPISODE units against the same two comparators with the same 0.08 threshold and the same collision gate

the frozen checkpoint selection contract ALREADY ranks by 'minimize recoverability Brier score', which presupposes a probabilistic output; option C moves the target toward the existing frozen selection authority rather than away from it
it emits exactly one scalar per candidate, which is what a decentralized runtime can rank locally
no threshold in its definition is taken from the observed V2 failure
why_not_A: a workable abstention needs the boundary events as supervision, so it collapses into B; and pure deletion cannot teach a runtime when to abstain
why_not_B: defining the boundary class as 'mixed replicas' makes class membership a function of R rather than of the state, and the statistically justified variant needs R >= 27
why_not_D: it requires per-event precision (R >= 27 for +/-0.20, R >= 104 for +/-0.10) and its two constants q and the confidence level have no independent repository rationale
